title: Enterprise request normalizer and bounded-scope pipeline
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Sales and CS receive high-volume, freeform enterprise feature asks. Current manual triage creates a backlog, inconsistent scope sizing, and varying signals sent to Eng/Design. Goal: build an intake normalizer + bounded-scope pipeline that automatically extracts structured fields, applies a lightweight scoring rubric, and emits a suggested 'first-pass scope' envelope (technical fit, priority band, rough engineering size band). This reduces time-to-first-scope and enables rapid routing to the right team.

Scope:
- Define canonical intake schema (problem statement, business metric, affected surfaces, required compliance, desired timeline, known blockers, value estimate) and normalization rules for freeform text.
- Implement a lightweight scoring rubric (impact, effort, risk, strategic alignment) that maps to priority bands (P0-P3) and size bands (S, M, L).
- Create a fast auto-scope generator that produces a 1-paragraph scoped proposal and recommended next step (pilot, research spike, build) for the PM/SE reviewer.
- Integrate with CS workspace (Zendesk/Slack/Drive prototype) and surface signals in the Enterprise Intake dashboard.
- Pilot with three high-volume accounts for 4 weeks, iterate, then roll to broader CS.

Out of scope: full implementation of solution design or approvals, SLA-backed commitments, heavy-weight legal reviews.

Why this is different: existing intake playbooks focus on manual consolidation. This ticket emphasizes normalization and a bounded auto-scope envelope to make signals machine-readable and quickly actionable by PM and Eng while retaining human review before commitment.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical intake schema documented and published to Confluence with field-level examples
Automated normalizer extracts at least 6 structured fields from >70% of incoming enterprise asks during pilot
Scoring rubric produces priority+size bands that match PM reviewer judgement at least 75% of the time in pilot sampling
Auto-scope output includes a concise 2-4 sentence recommended scope envelope and next step; PM reviewers mark it useful in at least 70% of sampled cases
Integration demonstrates intake items appear in Enterprise Intake dashboard with normalized fields and scoring within 48 hours of submission
assumptions: CS will add the canonical intake form link to account playbooks for pilot customers
We can access a sample set of 180 past enterprise requests for training heuristics
No additional legal/compliance gating required for initial metadata extraction
Limited Eng involvement for pilot; full engineering build will be scoped in a follow-up ticket if pilot success criteria met
deliverables: Confluence doc: canonical intake schema and normalization rules (link in comments)
Prototype normalizer (script + mapping rules) and sample outputs
Scoring rubric document and evaluation script
Pilot run report with metrics and decision recommendation
Template for PM quick-scope message and CS handoff checklist
stakeholders: Rina Gupta - Head of Customer Success
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overconfident auto-scopes could misroute high-risk asks. Mitigation: always require human approval before any engineering commit.
Risk: Normalizer may perform poorly on edge-case language. Mitigation: include a confidence score and flag low-confidence items for manual review.
Risk: CS adoption friction. Mitigation: run 2-week shadow pilot with SEs, collect feedback, and iterate on the intake link placement and UX.
timeline: Week 0 (Feb 10-16): finalize schema, gather sample requests
Week 1 (Feb 17-23): build normalizer prototype and scoring rubric; ship Confluence doc
Week 2-5 (Feb 24-Mar 23): pilot with 3 accounts, collect metrics, weekly syncs
Week 6 (Mar 24-28): pilot retrospective and decision on broader rollout
notes: This ticket focuses on the first-pass automation layer. If pilot shows >75% alignment with PM judgement and reduces triage time by 30%, open a downstream Engineering project for production integration and a UI for PMs in the Console.
